title: SceneAxi open-path demo policy (v1)
description: The one canonical table saying how far each profile's open path may be demonstrated, and by what evidence. A product boundary, so it is a closed enumeration rather than a lookup with a default: a profile that is not listed refuses, and no row can be read as a shipping, publication, or production-readiness claim — shippingClaim is const false everywhere it appears. @sceneaxi/profile-kids stays refuse-only with an empty operation set. Mirrors packages/schemas/src/open-path-policy.ts OPEN_PATH_POLICY; pnpm check:contracts keeps the docs/open-path-policy.md table in exact lockstep with this file, and a seam test asserts the TypeScript table and this fixture are identical. Deliberately expressed in the JSON Schema subset scripts/check-contracts.mjs supports.

refuseOnlyProfile.description: The profile whose open-path policy is refusal. Named so no surface has to infer it, and asserted so it cannot quietly become driveable.

const.summary: Opens a composed multi-object scene kernel session offline; a development demo, not a shippable game.
Opens a single-object kernel session inside the locked Web Experience scope; a development demo, not a shipped website.
Refuses every shared engine open-path demo; the separate Kids origin allows only its curated in-memory activity, with no commerce, identity, external data, or model route.

profiles.description: The three exact v1 policy rows in canonical order. No other profile, demo level, session kind, operation, evidence path, duplicate, omission, or reordering is valid. Adding a profile is an explicit contract edit that moves this file, the TypeScript table, and the doc together.
